sarah_research: Heads-up — onboarding Gemma-v2 (hf/gemma-v2-large) on the qwen tokenizer + our usual rotary handling shows a consistent accuracy drop on the eval suite. Strange pattern: short-context QA is fine, but longer prompts (>1024) have hallucination spikes and logit drift around token positions 512-768.

oliver: Can you paste the minimal repro and the eval diff?

sarah_research: repro is tiny. I attach logs inline:
```
# run config
model: gemma-v2-large
tokenizer: qwen-v1
rotary_base: 10000  # our default
rotary_n: 64
quant: q4_k_m
sequence_length: 2048
```
Diff snippet (gold vs pred): token IDs around a phrase get shifted by +1 in the served pipeline. Looks like prefix length handling / BOS insertion mismatch between tokenizers.

emma_ml: +1 token id shift would definitely misalign rotary positions. Are we inserting a BOS or extra special token somewhere in the private runtime but not in hf tokenizer?

sarah_research: That’s my suspicion. On local hf tokenizer, tokenize('Hello') -> [50256, ...] but in our prod tokenizer it becomes [1, 50256, ...] (we use an internal sentinel). I tried forcing strip_special_tokens=true and the eval improved but still not back to baseline.

raj: Could also be rotary offset assumptions. If the KV cache indexing assumes no extra lead token, the sin/cos table applied to token i will drift. Two quick checks: 1) compare token IDs from both tokenizers on identical text; 2) replay kv cache indices at generation start to see if we apply a +1 offset anywhere.

sarah_research: Did both. Token streams differ (prod adds sentinel), and when I replayed kv indices, the rotary lookup used absolute position not position - lead_tokens. Quick hack: subtract 1 from positions when sentinel_detected => small improvement. But still some residual regression on quantized weights.

oliver: Residual after fixing offsets points to quantization sensitivity (q4_k_m). Did you run a float32 vs q4 compare on the same tokenization? Might be compounded: token shift + precision loss.

sarah_research: Yes — float32 + corrected offsets recovers nearly baseline. q4 still lags on long contexts (perplexity +10%). I ran a focal test: quantize_only_attention vs quantize_all. The attention-only quantized model behaves closer to float32.

ci-bot: CI run completed: branch=fix/positional-offsets, tests=unit+small-eval, status=amber. See: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234

emma_ml: Two follow-ups: 1) add explicit token normalization in our tokenizer wrapper to strip internal sentinels when running open-source models, OR 2) keep sentinels but shift rotary base and kv indexing consistently (preferable for private models). Which path do we want product-wise?

raj: For compatibility across builders, I'd go with option 1 as default (strip by default, opt-in keep). But for Dedicated/Private we need a config flag to preserve original behavior. Also add a regression test: feed a canonical prompt and assert logits within epsilon for positions 0..N for float vs serving pipeline.

sarah_research: I'll open two PRs: tokenizer-normalize + regression test, and a separate quant-smoke that runs float vs q4 on a few long-context seeds. Will also log the exact rotary index offsets applied during generation into the debug trace.

oliver: Nice. If you need a quick quant experiment, I can spin a gpu pool on Dedicated. ping me in thread and I'll attach run IDs. :thumbsup:

sarah_research: Thanks — will do. Attaching quick reproduce command for the record:
```bash
python eval_long_context.py --model gemma-v2-large --tokenizer qwen-v1 --strip-sentinel --quant none --seq 2048 --seed 42
python eval_long_context.py --model gemma-v2-large --tokenizer qwen-v1 --strip-sentinel --quant q4_k_m --seq 2048 --seed 42
```

raj: Also try toggling rotary_n (64 vs 32) and rotary_scale_factor — some models use different implicit scalings; add that matrix to the eval grid.

sarah_research: Will run grid tomorrow and post results. Thanks all.

ci-bot: Created issue #452: "positional-interop: gemma + qwen tokenizer sentinel causing rotary index drift" (assignee: sarah_research)
